record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Kakeya rotation property in three dimensions
record.original_question: Does there exist a convex body S in R^3 that fails the Kakeya rotation property, meaning that there is some convex S-Kakeya body K in R^3 containing congruent copies of S in every orientation, but not every two copies of S inside K can be continuously rotated into one another while remaining inside K?

evidence.quote: Question 9.2. Is there a convex body S in R3 which does not have the Kakeya rotation property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S be a convex body in R^3 (a compact convex set with non-empty interior). A convex body K ⊂ R^3 is called S-Kakeya if, for every rotation ρ ∈ SO(3), K contains a congruent copy ρ(S) + v of S (for some translation vector v depending on ρ). 

Say that S has the Kakeya rotation property if, for every convex S-Kakeya body K ⊂ R^3 and every two congruent copies S₁, S₂ of S contained in K, there exists a continuous path of congruent copies of S, all contained in K, starting at S₁ and ending at S₂ (so that any two copies of S inside K can be continuously rotated and translated into one another while remaining inside K).

Does there exist a convex body S in R^3 that fails the Kakeya rotation property? Equivalently, can one find S ⊂ R^3 and a convex S-Kakeya body K ⊂ R^3 containing two congruent copies of S that cannot be joined by a continuous family of congruent copies of S lying inside K?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Janzer, "Rotation inside convex Kakeya sets," Discrete & Computational Geometry 2024) establishes that in R^3 the stronger continuous-selection version of the rotation property fails even for a line segment, and that the (weaker) Kakeya rotation property fails in dimensions ≥ 4 for general S. However, for the weaker rotation property in R^3 with general convex S, the question appears to remain unresolved; for S a line segment in any dimension the weaker property is known to hold. No source found resolving the R^3 case for general convex S.

status_evidence.title: Rotation inside convex Kakeya sets
status_evidence.snippet: In R^3 the stronger continuous-selection property fails even for line segments; in dimension ≥4 the weaker rotation property fails for general S; in any dimension the weaker question is positive for line segments.
status_evidence.claim: The R^3 case for the weaker (Kakeya rotation) property with general convex S is not settled by this work.

status_evidence.title: Barnabás Janzer: Rotation inside convex Kakeya sets
status_evidence.snippet: Summary of Janzer's results across dimensions, leaving the 3-dimensional general-S case for the weaker property open.
status_evidence.claim: Public discussion of Janzer's paper indicates the R^3 weaker rotation property for general S remains open.
